title: Deterministic Minimum-Output-Entropy Nonadditivity via Haagerup's Inequality and Near-Free Permutation Representations
authors: Guocheng Zhen, Chengkai Zhu, Ranyiliu Chen, Xin Wang
abstract: We give a deterministic realization of the finite-dimensional quadratic certificate underlying Collins's mixed-unitary proof of minimum-output-entropy nonadditivity. For every fixed integer $K\ge 2$ and rational $η>0$ satisfying $\log K>2(3+η)^2$, a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, for every sufficiently large target size $N$, outputs $K$ permutations on $N'=N+o_{K,η}(N)$ points. Restricting their permutation matrices to the nontrivial standard representation yields real orthogonal Stinespring blocks and a channel $Φ_{N'}:M_{N'-1}(\mathbb{C})\to M_K(\mathbb{C})$ such that \[ 2H_{\min}(Φ_{N'}) -H_{\min}(Φ_{N'}^{\otimes 2}) \ge \frac{\log K}{K} -2\log\left(1+\frac{(3+η)^2}{K}\right) >0. \] The construction combines Haagerup's length-two inequality with the simultaneous deterministic spectral approximation of O'Donnell and Wu. We further show that the constant $3$ is asymptotically sharp on the relevant Hermitian zero-diagonal coefficient class and that the finite spectral transfer is nearly saturated, thereby isolating the finer geometry of the full output body as the natural next level of refinement beyond the scalar-radius method. Finally, a standard covariant extension converts the same deterministic entropy gap exactly into self-tensor superadditivity of the one-shot Holevo quantity.
summary: This work provides a deterministic, polynomial-time construction demonstrating the nonadditivity of minimum-output-entropy for quantum channels. By combining advanced inequalities like Haagerup's with spectral approximation techniques, the authors establish a positive entropy gap. This result is significant because it provides a rigorous, constructive proof that translates directly into superadditivity for the one-shot Holevo quantity.
main_problem: The paper addresses the deterministic realization of the quadratic certificate proving the nonadditivity of the minimum-output-entropy for quantum channels.
main_result: It constructs a deterministic, polynomial-time algorithm yielding a specific entropy gap for the channel, which is shown to translate exactly into superadditivity for the one-shot Holevo quantity.
method: The construction combines Haagerup's length-two inequality with the deterministic spectral approximation of O'Donnell and Wu, applied to channels realized via real orthogonal Stinespring blocks.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is a quantum channel $\Phi_{N'}:M_{N'-1}(\mathbb{C})	o M_K(\mathbb{C})$, whose properties are governed by its minimum-output-entropy ($H_{\min}$).
key_observables: Minimum output entropy ($H_{\min}$), the entropy gap $2H_{\min}(\Phi_{N'}) - H_{\min}(\Phi_{N'}^{\otimes 2})$, and the one-shot Holevo quantity ($\chi$).
important_parameters: Fixed integer $K \ge 2$, rational tolerance $\eta > 0$, and the asymptotic input size $N$.
main_assumptions: The construction is algorithmic and asymptotic, relying on the existence of a real Stinespring realization for the channels.
paper_structure: The paper develops the deterministic construction, proves the entropy gap inequality using spectral approximation, and concludes by showing the equivalence of this gap to superadditivity for the Holevo quantity.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, deterministic, and algorithmic proof of a fundamental non-additivity property in quantum information theory, advancing the understanding of channel capacity beyond simple random constructions.
